Per-Agent Artifacts keep governance amendments local instead

title: The copy of an Agent Artifact recorded in the Sky Atlas is canonical and prevails over any other version
content:
A.1.14.2.3 requires that "All Agent Artifacts, including new Agent Artifacts, must be recorded and publicly documented in the Agent Scope of the Sky Atlas." A.1.14.2.3.1 then settles what happens when copies drift: "While the text of Agent Artifacts may be copied and made accessible in other locations, the version... publicly documented within the Agent Scope of the Sky Atlas must be treated as canonical. In the event of any discrepancies between the Agent Artifact recorded in the Sky Atlas and elsewhere, the version formally documented in the Sky Atlas shall prevail."

The rule is permissive about distribution and absolute about authority, which is the correct combination. Agents will inevitably publish their own governance on their own sites and docs, and forbidding that would only push copies underground. What must not be ambiguous is which text binds.

The consequence falls on Agents rather than on readers. An Agent whose website says something different from the Agent Scope is not governed by its website — its participants may have relied on text that has no force. Keeping the mirror synchronized is the Agent's problem, and the Atlas gives them no defence based on their own published version.

This is also what makes the supremacy and conflict machinery operable. A conflict determination under A.1.14.1.5 needs a single authoritative text to compare against the Sky Core Atlas; without a canonical-version rule, an Agent could contest any finding by pointing at a differently worded copy.
description: Artifacts may be republished anywhere, but the Agent Scope version governs; discrepancies resolve in favour of the Atlas record.
